newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to award tender for iron works in November.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to award tender for iron works in November.

text.p: A contract for engineering, procurement, and construction work at Qatar's $400 million hot briqueted iron (HBI) facility will be awarded in November, officials said on Tuesday.

"So far Mexico's HYL along with the U.S. Kvaerner Metals and Germany's Lurgi along with the U.S. Midrex Company have submitted bids for the project," said an official at the state-owned Qatar Steel Company (QSC).
He said the bidding would be closed on Wednesday.
The project - Qatar Hot Briquetted Company (QABICO) - is designed to produce two million tonnes of iron a year, used to make molten steel, by the end of 1999.

QABICO is 31 percent owned by QSC, 10 percent each by Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Company and Qatar Shipping Company and 16.33 percent each by Gulf Investment Corporation of Kuwait, National Industries Company of Kuwait and Canada's Duferco Participation Holdings Ltd of Guernsey (Channel Islands).
The project, which will use Qatar's abundant natural gas to operate, will be funded 70 percent by syndicated loans and 30 percent by equity contribution.

Eight banks - the partly state-owned Qatar National Bank, Sumitomo Bank, Banque Paribas, Credit Suisse GSGZn.S, Chase Manhattan, ANZ Grindlays, Arab Banking Corporation and Gulf International Bank- have formed a consortium to arrange financing.

Officials said Duferco will buy 1.2 million tonnes a year of QABICO's production and QSC will take 400,000 tonnes a year for its own consumption. The remaining 400,000 will be sold on the international market.
